summary: Compare agricultural policy options, assess delivery constraints and draft a decision brief. Explore the five-day course and enrol with TrainingCred.
lede: Agricultural policy development turns sector evidence into workable public decisions. For policy officers, agricultural economists and rural development planners, the course supports the practical task of preparing a policy brief through sector diagnosis, comparison of policy options and assessment of effects across producer groups. It also covers public investment screening, implementation planning through a Theory of Change, and indicator selection, with climate pressures and evidence limitations in view.
audienceIntro: This foundation-level course is designed for professionals who contribute to agricultural policy design, appraisal or implementation and need to connect sector evidence with workable public decisions.
modules: Agricultural Policy Foundations and FAO Priorities
Agricultural Diagnosis and Value Chain Analysis
FAO Sustainable Food and Agriculture Approach
Theory of Change for Agricultural Delivery
SDG Alignment and Agricultural Policy Capstone
prerequisites: No prior policy-analysis qualification is required. Familiarity with agriculture, rural development, public administration or sector programming is useful.
